title: She carried her baby straight into the accusations.
subtitle: Maryam faces her people
then: Maryam accepted Allah's command and {idea}readily received His decree{/idea}. She took her child and brought him to her people. When they saw her, {trap}they made a big deal of it and protested sternly{/trap}: you have brought something terrible.
now: You have to walk into the family dinner where everyone has already heard a version of your story. Your stomach drops in the car park. {idea}Maryam walked in holding the very thing they would accuse her over, trusting Allah to speak for her.{/idea}
old: I cannot face people until I have every answer ready.
new: I can face people with trust in Allah, even before I can explain myself.
try: Face one conversation you have been avoiding, and say a short dua before you go in.

title: Sister of Harun, your family was never like this.
subtitle: They used her good family against her
then: They called her {idea}sister of Harun{/idea}, meaning one who resembled him in worship, or a descendant of his line. Then they said: you come from a pure family known for righteousness. {trap}How could you do such a thing?{/trap}
now: Someone says: your parents are such good people, how could you? It hurts more because it uses love as a weapon. {trap}They are judging the surface.{/trap} The full truth is not always visible to the people who talk the most.
old: If my respected family sees it badly, it must be bad.
new: People, even good ones, can judge wrongly when the truth is hidden from them.
try: Next time you hear a story about someone, hold your judgment until you know more.

title: She just pointed at the baby.
subtitle: Silence, then she hands the answer over
then: Maryam was fasting from speech, so she {idea}referred all speech to the child{/idea}. They thought she was playing with them. As-Suddi said they became angrier, saying her mocking them was worse than the accusation itself.
now: You did what you believed was right and now it looks ridiculous to everyone in the room. They laugh. {idea}Maryam's gesture looked foolish for a few seconds, right before Allah answered for her.{/idea}
old: If doing the right thing makes me look foolish, I should stop.
new: Trusting Allah can look foolish for a moment before it is proved right.
try: Do one right thing today even if someone might laugh at it.

title: The baby spoke: I am the servant of Allah.
subtitle: Isa's first words, from the cradle

key.label: His first words did two things

then: Ibn Kathir says Isa's first words declared {idea}the honor of his Lord and that Allah has no child{/idea}, and that he himself worshipped Allah. Saying Allah made him a Prophet was {reward}a declaration of his mother's innocence{/reward}.
now: You introduce yourself all the time: job title, city, whose son or daughter. {idea}Isa's very first words about himself were: servant of Allah.{/idea} Everything else came after that.
old: Who I am is my job, my family, my achievements.
new: The first and truest thing about me is that I am Allah's servant.
try: Before you start work today, remind yourself: I am Allah's servant first.

title: Blessed wherever I am, with prayer and charity for life.
subtitle: A blessing that travels with you
then: Mujahid explained blessed wherever I am as {reward}a teacher of goodness, a person of great benefit{/reward}. Wuhayb bin Al-Ward said his blessing was commanding good and forbidding evil wherever he was. Prayer and zakah were enjoined on him {idea}for his whole life{/idea}.
now: The new office. The hospital ward. The football club where you coach on Saturdays. {reward}Being blessed is not about things going well for you; it is about people being better off because you were there.{/reward}
old: I will be blessed when life gets easier for me.
new: I am blessed when I bring good to whatever place I am in.
try: In one place you go today, leave one small good behind: help, a kind word, a tidy space.

title: Dutiful to my mother, never a wretched tyrant.
subtitle: Worship of Allah paired with kindness to a mother
then: Isa said Allah commanded him to treat his mother well. Ibn Kathir notes this comes after obedience to Allah because {idea}Allah often joins worship of Him with kindness to parents{/idea}, as in Surah Al-Isra. Maryam had just endured everything for this child.
now: Your mother sacrificed in ways you probably never saw: the nights, the worries, what people said. {reward}Isa's words for his mother came in the same breath as his worship.{/reward} Your tone with her is part of your religion.
old: Being religious is about prayer; family is a separate thing.
new: Kindness to my mother is joined to my worship of Allah.
try: Do one thing for your mother today without being asked, or make dua for her by name.

title: Peace on me at birth, at death, and when raised.
subtitle: Isa echoes the peace given to Yahya

key.label: What was true of his birth

then: The baby finished his words: peace on the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised. The people had just called his birth {trap}a terrible thing{/trap}. {reward}Allah called it a day of peace.{/reward}
now: Someone has written a story about you: the gossip at work, the label from school. It sticks. {reward}What people call your story and what Allah calls it can be completely different.{/reward}
old: What people say about my life is the final word on it.
new: Allah's word on my life outweighs every rumor about it.
try: Let go of one label someone gave you, and ask Allah for peace on your three days.

title: That is Isa, son of Maryam: the word of truth.
subtitle: The story told plainly, after all the dispute
then: Allah tells Muhammad ﷺ: this is the story of Isa. Ibn Kathir says it is {idea}a statement of truth{/idea}, about which the people of truth and falsehood disagree. In Surah Al Imran: the truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
now: You read ten threads about something important and each one says something different. Your head spins. {idea}This verse plants a flag: here is the truth from Allah, said simply.{/idea}
old: With so many opinions, I can never know what is true.
new: Allah has told the truth plainly; I can hold onto it amid the noise.
try: Close one argument thread you are scrolling today and read a page of Quran instead.

title: No son for Allah: He says Be, and it is.
subtitle: Glory to Him, above what is said about Him
then: After showing Isa as servant and Prophet, Allah {idea}glorifies Himself{/idea}: it does not befit Him to take a son. Whenever He wants something, He commands it and it happens. Ibn Kathir links this to Surah Al Imran: Isa is like Adam, created from dust with the word Be.
now: You picture Allah through human limits: tired, needing help, needing heirs. {idea}He needs nothing.{/idea} The plans you are worried about are, for Him, one word.
old: Allah works the way people work, with limits and needs.
new: Allah needs no one; He says Be, and it is.
try: Say subhanallah slowly ten times today, thinking about what it means.

title: Allah is my Lord and your Lord: worship Him.
subtitle: Isa's message, the straight path
then: Among what Isa said from the cradle: {idea}Allah is my Lord and your Lord{/idea}, so worship Him alone. Ibn Kathir explains: what I bring from Allah is the straight path. Whoever follows it is guided.
now: Prayer time, and you are next to a stranger at the airport prayer room. Different language, different background. {idea}Same Lord.{/idea} The straight path is simple enough to say in one sentence.
old: Faith is complicated and only experts can find the right path.
new: The straight path is clear: one Lord for all of us, worship Him.
try: Pray your next prayer remembering: He is my Lord and the Lord of everyone praying with me.

title: Then factions split, even after it was made clear.
subtitle: Disagreement after clarity, and a great Day ahead
then: Ibn Kathir says opinions about Isa differed {trap}even after his affair was explained{/trap}. The warning of the great Day is for those who lie about Allah. Yet Allah {idea}gives respite{/idea}; the Prophet ﷺ said no one is more patient with hurtful words than Allah, who still provides for them.
now: You already know the right thing in some area of your life, but you keep arguing yourself out of it. {idea}Allah's patience with you is real.{/idea} It is time given, not permission.
old: Since nothing has happened to me, it must not matter.
new: Allah's delay is patience and a chance to return, not a sign that He does not see.
try: Pick one thing you know is right but keep putting off, and start it today.

title: On that Day everyone will see and hear clearly.
subtitle: Clear sight that comes too late
then: Ibn Kathir says on the Day of Resurrection the wrongdoers will have the clearest hearing and sight, saying: our Lord, now we have seen and heard. {trap}But it will not help them then.{/trap} {reward}If they had used these senses before, it would have benefited them.{/reward}
now: The day after the argument, you see clearly what you should have said. After the diagnosis, you see the warnings. {reward}This verse asks you to use your eyes and ears now, while seeing still changes something.{/reward}
old: I will think about the big questions later.
new: Clarity is only useful while I still have time to act on it.
try: Ask yourself honestly today: what am I choosing not to see?

title: Warn of the Day of Regret, while people are heedless.
subtitle: When the matter is decided for good
then: The Prophet ﷺ described death brought between Paradise and the Fire and slaughtered, with eternity declared for both. Then he recited this verse and said: {trap}the people of this life are in heedlessness of this life.{/trap} Ibn Mas'ud said every soul will see a home in each.
now: Notifications, deadlines, the next episode starting in five seconds. {trap}Heedlessness rarely feels like rejecting anything.{/trap} It feels like being busy. {reward}The door is still open today.{/reward}
old: I am not rejecting anything; I am just busy.
new: Busy distraction is the heedlessness this verse warns about, and today I can still choose.
try: Turn off autoplay or one notification today and use those minutes to remember Allah.

title: Allah inherits the earth and all on it.
subtitle: Everything returns to its true Owner
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is the Creator, Owner and Controller of all. {idea}All creation will pass and only He remains.{/idea} He judges, and no soul will be wronged even an atom's weight. Umar bin Abdul-Aziz quoted this verse in a letter to his governor.
now: The house deeds with your name on them. The inheritance argument in the family. {idea}Every name on every title deed is temporary.{/idea} The One who inherits it all is also the One who judges fairly.
old: What I have built and own is mine to keep.
new: Everything I hold returns to Allah; I am only looking after it for a while.
try: Give away or lend one thing you own today, remembering it was never fully yours.
